messages:
Carla Nguyen: heads-up — ran quick bring-up for Argus11B. need product/GTN guidance on quant tradeoffs before we push to canary. TL;DR: int8 looks promising on latency/cost but we see sporadic recall drops on long-dialog slices.
Sam Choi: can you paste the exact slices where recall dropped?
Carla Nguyen: sure — short excerpt: 
```
slice: long-multi-turn-support
metrics: rougeL 0.42 -> 0.36 (fp16 -> int8)
regressions on follow-up Qs and entity consistency
```

Jordan K: did you run the hybrid-int6 baseline? that usually reduces regressions with modest cost bump. numbers?
Carla Nguyen: ran fp16 / int8 / int6 hybrid. quick numbers per 1k tokens (in our env): fp16 ~ $0.95, int8 ~ $0.32, hybrid-int6 ~ $0.45. tail-latency p95: fp16 240ms, int8 160ms, hybrid 180ms.
Priya Sharma: thanks. For GTN, product cares about two things: 1) unit cost delta vs quality drop (esp for multi-turn), 2) predictable fallbacks. Do we have a simple rule-of-thumb for routing?
Sam Choi: suggestion: default int8 for non-multi-turn routes (search, short completion), hybrid-int6 for chat-heavy routes, fallback to fp16 for critical flows. implement via routing flag: model_variant:intX per-route.
Carla Nguyen: noted. small ops note: int8 shows ~7% more memory contention on our host during high conc, leading to occasional OOMs on 32k contexts. int6 hybrid reduces that.
ml-onboard-bot: bench summary uploaded: https://internal/bench/argus11b/1776543210 — artifacts: logs, token-cost breakdown, slice-diffs.
Jordan K: Priya — what's acceptable quality loss for GTN? earlier guidance was <=3% relative metric drop on critical slices. this is ~6-7% on those long-turn slices.
Priya Sharma: that's above threshold. But product can accept 6% if cost delta >2.5x and fallbacks are automatic. Recommend: canary with traffic split 80% int8, 18% hybrid-int6, 2% fp16 for high-risk users. Monitor recall and start canary only after adding KV-prefetch to reduce context fetch variance.
Sam Choi: ops checklist for canary: 1) add prefetched KV cache for multi-turn routes, 2) enable automatic rollback at 3% overall regressions on slice set, 3) per-user sticky routing to avoid flip-flop. I'll open a runbook PR.
Carla Nguyen: action items: I'll prepare a concise scorecard for GTN with cost/unit, p95 latency, slice delta, and recommended route per product route. also include a simple traffic-split config snippet.
Priya Sharma: sounds good. please include a comparison table (fp16 / hybrid-int6 / int8) and an explicit rollback threshold. I'll take this to GTN sync.
Carla Nguyen: putting the scorecard draft in the bench artifacts and pinging product. thanks all :thumbsup:
ml-onboard-bot: runbook PR created: https://internal/pulls/1023 — includes canary config and rollback thresholds.
Sam Choi: I'll seed the canary tomorrow morning EST and watch the first 30m slice metrics.
Jordan K: if we see noisy signals, prefer conservative rollback rather than fiddling with quant profiles mid-canary.
Carla Nguyen: agreed. closing loop here, will share final doc and tl;dr for GTN.
